name: A crash between COMMIT and the enqueue wedges a whole head, and nothing recovers it
description:
Raised out of CZ3TDR1-739 / PR #78, where Copilot flagged it on both worker paths. The limitation is documented in the code and was accepted deliberately when the sends moved after the commit — but the decision only lived in a summary file, so nothing tracked it. This is that ticket.

## The window

Three paths now commit their `reviews` rows and enqueue the pg-boss jobs afterwards: the poll fan-out (`ensureReviewsForPull`), triage's cheap/scout branch, and the judge insert. If the process dies after COMMIT and before the send — a deploy, an OOM kill, a SIGKILL — the rows are durable and no job names them. The compensation that would drop them is in a `catch` that a dead process never reaches.

**It is permanent, not delayed.** Nothing reaps a stale `queued` row; the console requeues only `failed`/`rejected`; `reviewExists` makes every later triage skip that provider; and `reviews_repo_pr_head_provider_uq` refuses a re-insert. So the head's barrier never fires, `/rereview` reads it as settled, and it stays that way until someone deletes the row by hand. `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md` has the manual recovery, under "Řádek uvízlý v `queued`, pro který neexistuje job".

## What is and is not new

Not new: a send that _failed_ used to leave exactly this state, because the old code had no compensation at all. The shape is the same.

New: the count. A crash between an insert and its send used to strand that one row and simply never create the rest; now every row of the head is durable and none of them has a job. A wedged head is a wedged head either way, but an operator counting rows should expect the whole fan-out rather than one row.

Also worth knowing: this is the one shape on these paths that no retry repairs. A send that merely _fails_ is handled — the compensation drops the rows whose jobs did not go out, and the caller's retry rebuilds them.

## The fix, and why it was not folded into #78

**The enqueue has to commit with the rows instead of after them.** pg-boss 12 supports this directly: `send`'s options take a `db` (`ConnectionOptions.db?: IDatabase`), and with it the job insert runs as statements on the caller's handle rather than in pg-boss's own transaction — its own source says so at the insert path ("db (options.db) we run the statements inline so they compose inside the caller's transaction"), and it puts its `pg_notify` in the same batch for exactly this reason. That is a transactional outbox: the row and its job commit together or neither does, the compensations disappear, and this window closes.

It stayed out of #78 for three reasons, all of them still true:

1. The ticket, the brief and the docblock #74 left behind all prescribe post-commit dispatch. Substituting a different design late in that PR would have been a decision taken past the point anyone was reviewing it.
2. It needs an adapter from a drizzle transaction to pg-boss's `IDatabase` (`executeSql(text, values)`), on the poll's hot path. pg-boss passes pre-interpolated SQL there, so the adapter runs it raw — workable, but it is new plumbing rather than a smaller diff.
3. It moves the queue write inside the critical section that PR #78 exists to keep short, and it rewrites what every caller's failure path means. Both deserve their own review.

Nothing about it is blocked, and the dispatch is already isolated in one loop per path, so the change is contained.

## Scope

- `apps/worker/src/jobs/poll-partners.ts` — the fan-out's dispatch loop and its compensation
- `apps/worker/src/jobs/triage.ts` — the scout branch's send and its compensation
- `apps/worker/src/jobs/review-pr.ts` — `maybeEnqueueJudge`'s insert and its orphan delete
- the `JobSink` interface the first two take, which would have to carry the transaction

The three compensations and their tests go away with it; check what each test was actually pinning before deleting it, because two of them also assert identity of the rows left standing.

## Urgency

Lower than it sounds, and worth stating so nobody reprioritises on the wrong reading: the failure needs the process to die inside a window of a few statements, and the consequence is one PR that stops being reviewed rather than anything published wrongly or lost. It is visible in the console as a head that never settles. The reason to do it is that it is the only unrecoverable state left on these paths, not that it fires often.

**Done when:** a row and its job commit in one transaction on all three paths, the post-commit compensations are gone, and a test covers the case the compensations used to — that a failure at enqueue time leaves no row without a job.
